## Historical audit: S0078

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_regression_guidance/C1/selection/commons_133800864/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 is available; the referenced images are not visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal and initial build | The student was instructed to reconstruct a photograph as separate Blender meshes, matching camera and framing. Its code interpreted the scene as a kitchen with window, cabinet, towel, counter, sink and appliances; those semantic identifications are the student’s observations, not independently verified image content. The program constructs multiple groups, procedural granite and cloth/paper bump materials, lighting and a camera. [S0078, line 19, model request, characters 0–187739] |
| First revision | After the step-1 render, the student reported that a foreground wall obscured the window and objects appeared too small. It shortened the wall, changed lens 48 to 61 and retargeted the camera; it also parented the custom towel and jug-shoulder meshes to their semantic roots. The reported visual diagnosis is not independently checked here. [Line 19, characters 0–187739] |
| Second revision | The student reported exposed blinds but a cabinet bottom too low and towel too far left. Its **hypothesis** was that cabinet architecture, rather than global camera scale, caused the largest remaining disagreement. It raised and deepened the cabinet, changed its end and doors, shifted the towel assembly and adjusted paper brackets while retaining the step-2 camera. [Line 19, characters 0–187739] |
| Validation and selection | The embedded results report successful renders for steps 1 and 2; step 3 separately reports `ok: true`, a completed 16-sample render and saved blend/image. The runner initially selected step 3; after receiving the reference and three render paths, the student responded `SELECT 2`, and the runner selected step 2. No rationale for that final choice is visible. [Lines 17 [0,45928), 18 [0,58), 19 [0,187739), 21 [0,379), 22 [0,58)] |
| Guidance and exploration | The student received general review instructions after renders: check framing, coverage and contacts, and isolate a correction family. Its subsequent revisions visibly follow that procedure, but the supplied text contains no separate teacher-specific detection, diagnosis or proposed fix, nor evidence of receipt or adoption of such a fix. The student’s own diagnoses and revisions are visible; the final session recorded zero tool calls. [Lines 19 [0,187739), 20 [0,4486)] |

**Scene checks and outcome.** Code establishes multiple modeled objects and materials, but names and render logs do not establish their visible appearance. The custom meshes were parented from step 2; geometric connection, support contacts, pose, occlusion, lighting quality and camera match remain unverified. The student’s wall-occlusion and cabinet diagnoses remain claims, not independent visual findings. The runner’s successful executions and final selection are formal operational success; **reconstruction correctness is unknown**, not proven partial correctness or algorithm failure. No technical interruption or empty patch is shown.

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, separating camera/framing changes from later local geometry edits makes revisions easier to attribute, though the first revision also changed wall geometry. Specifically, whether raising the cabinet improved or regressed the kitchen reconstruction—and why step 2 was selected—cannot be established without the images or an explicit comparison. Earlier unseen events and any teacher interaction outside this chunk remain unknown.
